title: First vs Second Conditional: Real vs Imaginary
grammarTitle: First vs Second Conditional — Real vs Imaginary
grammarNote: Первое условное предложение (First Conditional) описывает РЕАЛЬНЫЕ, ВЕРОЯТНЫЕ ситуации в будущем. Второе (Second Conditional) — ВООБРАЖАЕМЫЕ, МАЛОВЕРОЯТНЫЕ или НЕРЕАЛЬНЫЕ. Выбор между ними определяет то, насколько реальным говорящий считает условие.

grammarTable.subject: First Conditional
grammarTable.example: "If you study hard, you will pass." (real plan, likely to happen)

grammarTable.subject: Second Conditional
grammarTable.example: "If you studied harder, you would pass." (imaginary — you're not studying hard)

grammarTable.subject: 1st: real future
grammarTable.example: "If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay in." (possible future — might rain)

grammarTable.subject: 2nd: not real now
grammarTable.example: "If it rained every day, I'd move away." (imaginary — it doesn't rain every day)

grammarTable.subject: 1st: open condition
grammarTable.example: "If I have time this weekend, I'll go to the museum." (maybe I'll have time)

grammarTable.subject: 2nd: closed (not real)
grammarTable.example: "If I had time, I'd go to the museum." (I don't have time — it's imaginary)

grammarExtra.title: The key difference: how LIKELY is the situation?

rows.example: "If she applies, she might get in." (She might apply — it's possible)
"If she applied, she might get in." (She probably won't apply — imaginary)
1st: Real possibility. 2nd: The speaker doesn't expect it to happen.

rows.form: Test: Do you expect it to happen?
rows.example: Probably YES → First Conditional. Probably NO / imaginary → Second Conditional.

grammarExtra.title: Compare the two: same situation, different meaning

rows.form: "If I have money, I'll go to Scotland."
rows.example: 1st Conditional → I might get money. This is a real plan.

rows.form: "If I had money, I'd go to Scotland."
rows.example: 2nd Conditional → I don't have money. This is a dream/wish.

rows.form: "If I see him, I'll tell him."
rows.example: 1st → I might see him (real possibility). I'll pass the message.

rows.form: "If I saw him, I'd tell him."
rows.example: 2nd → I don't expect to see him (imaginary). Dream scenario.

grammarExtra.title: Mixed signals — watch the tense carefully

rows.example: "If I GO to Almaty, I'll visit the museum." (1st — I might go)
"If I WENT to Almaty, I'd visit the museum." (2nd — I'm not going)
"If I have time, I WILL help you." (real — I might have time)
"If I had time, I WOULD help you." (imaginary — I don't have time)
"If you heat water to 100°C, it boils." (always true — scientific fact)
"If I miss the bus, I walk." (my regular habit — always true for me)
Zero → always. First → possible. Second → imaginary.
Zero: "If water freezes, it expands." / 1st: "If it freezes tonight, I'll be careful." / 2nd: "If I lived in Alaska, I'd be used to cold."

grammarTip:
Три условных предложения — как выбрать:
① ZERO: always true / general fact → if + Present, Present
"If you mix red and blue, you get purple."
② FIRST: real possibility in the future → if + Present, WILL
"If it rains, I'll take an umbrella."
③ SECOND: imaginary / unlikely → if + Past, WOULD
"If it rained every day, I'd move to the desert."

💡 Главный вопрос: "Насколько это реально?"
→ Возможно на самом деле = First Conditional
→ Воображаемо / маловероятно = Second Conditional

⚠️ Та же ситуация — разное значение:
"If I HAVE money, I'LL go." = У меня могут появиться деньги (реально).
"If I HAD money, I'D go." = У меня нет денег (воображаемо).

exercises.text: "If Kamila ___ hard, she ___ the exam." (she is currently studying — it's likely)
exercises.hint: She IS studying → it's realistic → FIRST Conditional. "If she STUDIES, she WILL PASS." ✅

exercises.text: "If Rustam ___ a car, he ___ drive everywhere." (he doesn't have one — imaginary)
exercises.hint: He doesn't have a car → imaginary → SECOND Conditional. "If he HAD a car, he WOULD DRIVE." ✅

exercises.text: "If I see Amir tomorrow, I'll give him the book."
exercises.hint: "If I SEE Amir" = I might see him (real possibility) → FIRST Conditional. "see" (present) + "will give". ✅

exercises.text: "If I saw Amir tomorrow, I'd give him the book."
exercises.hint: "If I SAW Amir" = I don't expect to see him (imaginary) → SECOND Conditional. "saw" (past) + "would give". ✅

exercises.text: She hasn't applied to Edinburgh. She says: "If I ___ there, my English ___ improve a lot."
exercises.hint: She's not going → imaginary → SECOND Conditional. "If I WENT there, my English WOULD improve." ✅

exercises.instruction: What is the difference in meaning?
exercises.text: "If she applies, she'll get in." vs "If she applied, she'd get in."
opts: 1st = she might apply (real); 2nd = she won't apply (imaginary)
exercises.correct: 1st = she might apply (real); 2nd = she won't apply (imaginary)
exercises.hint: 1st = possible/likely. 2nd = imaginary/unlikely. Same situation — different reality.

exercises.text: "If the weather ___ (be) good this weekend, we ___ (go) hiking." (real plan)
exercises.hint: Real plan — might happen → FIRST Conditional. "If the weather IS good, we WILL GO hiking." ✅

exercises.text: "If the weather ___ (be) always sunny in Uralsk, I ___ (not / leave)." (imaginary)
exercises.hint: Imaginary (weather is not always sunny) → SECOND. "If the weather WERE sunny, I WOULDN'T LEAVE." ✅

opts: "If I see her, I'll say hello."
exercises.hint: Zero Conditional = always true / scientific fact. "If + present, present." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence for a "real plan".
exercises.text: Kamila is thinking about applying for the scholarship. She says:
exercises.hint: Real plan (she might apply) → FIRST Conditional: if + present → will. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct sentence for a "dream scenario".
exercises.text: Amir doesn't have the money to start a company. He says:
opts: "If I have funding, I'll start a company."
"If I had funding, I'd start a company."
"If I have funding, I'd start a company."
"If I had funding, I'll start a company."
exercises.correct: "If I had funding, I'd start a company."
exercises.hint: Dream (he doesn't have funding) → SECOND Conditional: if + past → would. ✅

exercises.instruction: What does "If I see him" vs "If I saw him" tell us?
exercises.text: "If I SEE him, I'll tell him." vs "If I SAW him, I'd tell him."
opts: 1st: I might see him; 2nd: I don't expect to see him
exercises.correct: 1st: I might see him; 2nd: I don't expect to see him
exercises.hint: "If I SEE" = might happen (1st). "If I SAW" = unlikely/imaginary (2nd). Same words — different expectation!

questions.text: "If I have time, I'll help you." — This is:
"If I had time, I'd help you." — This is:
questions.hint: "had" (past) + "would help" → SECOND Conditional. Imaginary — I don't have time.

questions.text: First Conditional is used when the situation is:
questions.hint: 1st Conditional = real possibility. "If it rains, I'll take an umbrella." (It might rain)

questions.text: Second Conditional is used when the situation is:
questions.hint: 2nd Conditional = imaginary / unlikely. "If I were rich, I'd buy a house." (I'm not rich)

questions.text: "If ___ (rain), I'll cancel the trip." vs "If ___ (rain), I'd cancel."
questions.hint: 1st: if + PRESENT. 2nd: if + PAST. "If it RAINS" (1st) / "If it RAINED" (2nd).

questions.text: "If I ___ (study) abroad, I would improve faster." (imaginary)
questions.hint: Imaginary → 2nd Conditional → Past Simple in if-clause: "If I STUDIED abroad..." ✅

questions.text: "If she ___ (get) the scholarship, she ___ (move) to Edinburgh."
questions.hint: Real possibility (she might get it) → FIRST. "If she GETS the scholarship, she WILL MOVE." ✅

questions.text: "If water freezes, it expands." — This is:
questions.hint: Scientific/general truth → Zero Conditional. Both verbs = Present Simple. ✅

questions.text: What is the key question to decide between 1st and 2nd Conditional?
opts: How likely is the situation to happen?
questions.correct: How likely is the situation to happen?
questions.hint: Likely/possible → 1st. Unlikely/imaginary → 2nd. The key is reality vs imagination.

questions.text: "If she applied, she'd get in." — The speaker thinks:
questions.hint: 2nd Conditional = imaginary/unlikely. "If she APPLIED" (past) → speaker doesn't expect it.

questions.text: "If I have the money, I'll go." vs "If I had the money, I'd go." — Choose the IMAGINARY one.
questions.hint: "If I HAD" (past) = 2nd Conditional = imaginary. I don't have the money.

questions.text: "If she ___ (not / be) so busy, we ___ (see) her more." (imaginary)
questions.hint: Imaginary → 2nd. "If she WEREN'T so busy, we WOULD SEE her more." ✅

questions.text: A friend is encouraging you to study. They say:
questions.hint: Encouragement = real possibility = 1st Conditional. "If you STUDY, you WILL PASS." ✅

questions.text: You are discussing a dream. You say:
opts: "If I win the lottery, I'll travel."
"If I won the lottery, I'd travel."
questions.correct: "If I won the lottery, I'd travel."
questions.hint: Dream/unlikely → 2nd Conditional. "If I WON the lottery, I'D TRAVEL." ✅

questions.text: What does the if-clause tense signal?
opts: The exact time in the future
questions.hint: Present in if-clause = likely (1st). Past in if-clause = imaginary (2nd). The tense signals reality.

questions.text: Select the correct set of forms.
opts: Zero: if + present, present | 1st: if + past, will | 2nd: if + present, would
Zero: if + present, present | 1st: if + present, will | 2nd: if + past, would
questions.correct: Zero: if + present, present | 1st: if + present, will | 2nd: if + past, would
